title: Inside Track

summary.short: Bin follows the cellar trail and turns gossip into a usable lead.
summary.default: The Mug cellar yields a name, a courier route, and a quiet alliance with the host. Bin decides whether to bring it to the town meeting or hold it inside the family for one more night.

nodes.text: The Frosted Mug cellar runs cold. Two barrels. One trapdoor. A walking-around stain on the floor that is not from spilled ale, and a tally chalked on the back of a brick that nobody wants to claim drew it. The lantern keeps swinging by half a hair like the cellar is listening to its own breathing.

nodes.speaker: Tavern Host
nodes.text: If you are here for the ghosts, the ghosts left an hour ago. If you are here for the inquiries, sit down before I lose my nerve. I should have told someone weeks ago. I told my husband. He told me to wait. He is the kind of man who waits.

nodes.speaker: Peri
nodes.text: Listen to her. She is the most honest cowardice in this entire town. That is a compliment. It is the kind of compliment the system files under 'useful.' I am very fond of her. Do not tell her — she will use it as an excuse to feed me.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: Tell me what happened in your own order, not mine. I am not the law and I am not in a hurry. The system can wait, the town can wait, you cannot. I will not write a single word down until you are ready to lend it to me.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: Sorry. I almost said something stupid. Take your time. The cellar is not on fire. Please tell me before the cellar is on fire. I would like at least one indoor location in my life that is not currently in the process of catching.

nodes.speaker: Tavern Host
nodes.text: A courier comes on market days. Comes in on the south gate, asks two questions about Garr's hut, leaves three silver, leaves. Never twice in a row. Never says a name. Pays in coin nobody recognizes. Last visit was six days ago. They always order the cider they do not drink. I think it is a signal.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: Two questions about Garr's hut. Which two? The kind of questions tells you what the buyer is shopping for. Hours? People? Locks? The shape of the kitchen door?

nodes.speaker: Tavern Host
nodes.text: First question: when does Lily walk the dog at dawn. Second question: who has the key to the back garden. The first one made me sick. The second one made me write the tally on the brick because I needed to count something with my hands.

nodes.prompt: How does Bin handle the courier lead?

choices.label: Plan to bring this to the town meeting
choices.summary: Share with Frostbitten openly. Lower danger, more eyes on the route.

ops.text: Bin agreed to surface the courier at the town meeting.

choices.label: Keep it inside the family first
choices.summary: Quiet. Costs trust with the gate later if discovered, but the buyer does not hear it yet.

ops.text: Bin chose to keep the courier lead inside Garr's circle for now.

nodes.speaker: Tavern Host
nodes.text: Thank you. I will not stop you, but I will warn you. The courier has Frostbitten friends. People will not be glad to hear their names said out loud at a town meeting. Some of those names rent rooms upstairs.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: Names get said. The town owes itself the truth. We can leave the buyer's name off the room key for one more market day. After that, the courier shops somewhere else or the town learns who is renting eyes inside its walls.

nodes.speaker: Tavern Host
nodes.text: Family it is. I owe you the names, and I owe Garr two of them. Take them home, decide what stays inside the walls. I will keep the cider order for the next market day so the signal does not go cold.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: Family decides by tomorrow. If the family does not act, the meeting hears it on its own — too late. I am not interested in becoming the kind of person who keeps secrets longer than a market week. The math gets ugly fast.

nodes.speaker: Peri
nodes.text: Good. Now we walk you home before this turns into a domestic emergency. The town meeting is the next chapter no matter which fork you took. Try to arrive with both hands free. Try not to arrive bleeding. Try, in short, to arrive.
